cells: DRAFT & FINAL REVIEW  |  One complete teacher draft → feedback → student's revisions → final self-check
School guide: IA is worth 20% of course grade; assessment A Presentation /4, B Mathematical Communication /4, C Personal Engagement /3, D Reflection /3, E Use of Mathematics /6.
Show this at two real milestones: BEFORE the fully completed draft for teacher written feedback, and again BEFORE final submission. Do NOT show a 20-item checklist after every page.
2025 JIS guidance: approximately 12–20 pages and double line spacing are recommendations to verify against current school requirements; never treat length/spacing as an IB mark guarantee.
Students normally receive ONE round of written teacher feedback on a complete draft; other teacher feedback should be verbal and noted. The Pathfinder is not a submission or automatic marker.
Keep the essential default questions short and give a detailed optional checklist. Allow Save/Resume without declaring a draft or final IA ready; don't invent teacher deadlines.
Is the IA genuinely COMPLETE enough for a useful single written feedback round?
Aim/introduction, relevant methods/data or theory, maths, integrated figures, reflection and conclusion
Finish missing essential section and reread the whole exploration
Show near actual school draft milestone
Can the reader follow the investigation logically without irrelevant or repeated work?
Clear introduction with aim, coherent unfolding mathematics and conclusion
Remove repetition, clarify connections between stages, keep helpful diagrams beside text
Criterion check, not a predicted 0–4 mark
Are mathematical variables/terms, notation, units, equations and figures used clearly and correctly?
Equation editor, definitions at first use, credible accuracy, ≈ for rounded values, titled visuals
Jump to the precise equation/figure requiring repair
Only show detailed notation checklist on request/error
Does the work demonstrate OWNERSHIP through purposeful choices, conjectures and a personal perspective?
Student's aim and reasons, independently chosen investigations, authentic changes of direction
Strengthen genuine decision rationale where student actually made a choice
No invented personal history or artificial creative flourish
Have I reflected throughout, not just collected generic limitations in my conclusion?
Actual results interpreted, expectations revisited, mathematical methods evaluated in place, meaningful next questions
Return to result/method where reflection is missing, leave conclusion as synthesis
Is my ACTUAL mathematics relevant, appropriate for my course, correct and UNDERSTOOD?
Substantial, purposeful course-level mathematics; justified modelling or inference, explained technology use
Revise/select purpose-driven maths or discuss suitability with teacher
No guarantee that adding more techniques increases marks
Have I printed or closely inspected the WHOLE draft as a reader would see it?
Single-page graphs, legible equations, captions, page breaks, coherent margins
Fix specific clutter/oversized or split figure before teacher reads
Don't inspect only on zoomed screen
Could a classmate follow the mathematical decisions? Could a non-mathematician follow the story?
Peer or relative's confusion points, if available
Ask one reader to flag unclear jumps; revise in own words
Optional; does not require sharing private participant data
Are datasets, claims, graphics, quotations and outside mathematics correctly cited?
Consistent in-text citation and bibliography or works-cited, traceable URLs/publishers
Add missing attributions before submitting draft/final
School 2025 guide suggests MLA in Google Docs; follow current teacher-approved style consistently
Have I checked current school instructions for title page, spacing, approximate length and page numbering?
The 2025 guide suggests ~12–20 pages, double spacing; current policies may differ
Check current requirements; no invented deadline or absolute page-limit gate
Have I included substantial calculations/figures, not only a plan and placeholders?
Real calculations, purpose and interpretation near results
Finish mathematical body rather than treating intention as completed work
Teacher draft must be complete; data not assumed from plan
Is all analysis and reflection truly mine, with permissions and source credit?
Student authorship and sources; no unsupported AI-written IA passages
Revise unsupported passage, cite non-original sources, consult teacher when uncertain
Pathfinder must not auto-write final IA prose
Have I used the school's permitted written draft feedback opportunity appropriately?
One allowed teacher-written feedback round for completed IA
Record teacher feedback and action items; teacher controls advice
Never request a second round of written teacher feedback from this tool
When my teacher gives verbal advice, have I recorded what I need to do?
Short feedback note/action/date; distinguish suggestions from verified corrections
Act on relevant notes and re-check work
Do not let the tool impersonate teacher approval
Have I actually implemented the permitted feedback and checked the changes work?
Return to exact affected stage; preserve old notes and student writing
Don't auto-mark revisions done because feedback was imported
Can I identify the page or section where each criterion is genuinely evident?
Student-generated A–E evidence pointers, not automatic marks
Fix a genuine gap or note limitations; no predicted score
Criteria labels/scores are maxima, not guaranteed grade
Have I reread the final file, tested equation rendering, citations and figure placement?
Final print/PDF preview, spelling, grammar, page numbering
Correct local issue and recheck the final render
Not a submission action; cannot verify final file if not uploaded
Does the final cover page/identifier follow current school IB instructions?
Appropriate title, correct candidate identifier where required, no unapproved personal details
Ask teacher about identity, cover style and school submission method
Do not publish real participant names or assume one universal cover policy
IA Tips per topic; school requirements
Is the necessary evidence traceable without huge raw tables cluttering the IA?
Short meaningful examples/figures in body, dataset/source cited; optional justified supporting material
Default Pathfinder editorial preference: no long raw tables even in appendix; ask teacher if an exception is necessary for reproducibility
IB Guide ALLOWS justified large-data appendices; this is NOT an IB ban. Avoid redundant data tables.
Do calculator or software outputs show meaningful mathematical understanding?
Method name/inputs, purpose, interpretation, check of assumptions when needed
Explain mathematical reasoning at the point of use, not a tutorial
Show only for tools actually used
Is the correct school submission date/method confirmed, and am I ready to submit my own IA?
Actual student/school schedule and source-independent file
Follow school's process; no Pathfinder submission claim
No guessed dates or automated IB approval
TWO DISTINCT MILESTONES  |  The same Criteria A–E, but different timing and actions
Complete work; self-review A–E; proofread and print-read; cite sources.
Full draft required for meaningful ONE written feedback round.
Record allowed written feedback once, plus ongoing verbal notes and specific corrections.
Teacher's feedback is not automatically approval or a second review.
No editing student work on teacher's behalf.
Apply feedback, correct errors/graphs/equations and reflect as needed.
Use actual revised results rather than copied comments.
Preserve past version if student uses progress snapshot.
Run A–E evidence check again; print/PDF readability; proofreading; current deadline and process.
Save progress allowed without final readiness claim.
SELF-CHECK A–E  |  Show the concise question; detailed wording only if a student asks for it
Can someone follow my mathematical story, from clear aim to conclusion?
Coherence; relevant diagrams; no repetition; references.
Are the notation, definitions, diagrams, units and ≈/= precise and consistent?
Correct labels; proper mathematical symbols; appropriate accuracy.
Do my independent choices, conjectures and response to results show ownership?
Authentic motivation and investigation, not a fictional biography.
Did I reflect meaningfully as my mathematics unfolded?
Implications, limits, alternatives, justified changes, next questions.
Is the maths relevant, correct, understood and suitable for my IB course?
Substantial mathematical understanding, including technology where used.
Student seeks teacher written feedback with missing conclusion
Warn draft incomplete; offer jump to C60.
Do not label ready or require a particular IA heading template.
Student has completed a full teacher draft
Show concise review + A–E optional evidence; proceed to teacher process.
Do not offer automatic marking or send to teacher without explicit action.
Record notes and corrective actions; no second written-feedback suggestion.
Ask optional print-view/proofread and current deadlines/format.
Do not infer current deadline or declare authenticity checked.
Course-level maths only from prior learning
Criterion E flags need to reconsider actual maths with teacher.
Don't promise marks from simply adding complexity.
Suggest concise source link / justified evidence, state this is Pathfinder preference.
Don't label justified data appendices as IB-prohibited.
Student uses technology output without explanation
Prompt what method, why, what result means where performed.
Don't force full manual recalculation or a software tutorial.
Student's final presentation readable on computer but splits printed figure
Flag print/PDF check; recommend reflow to one page.
Don't shrink to illegibly small caption/axis text.
Student wants to save incomplete work
Don't mistake save snapshot for final IA submission.
REFERENCE: JIS SL Maths IA Guide 2025 (slides 2–6, 37, 40, 42–47 and 52); IB IA Checklist; IA Criterion Explained. Current school/teacher requirements take precedence where guidelines differ.
